scorecard.name: Branding and Survey Check
scorecard.coaching: At [00:00], you paraphrased the opening branding as 'thanks for calling S-Net' instead of 'thank you for calling S-Net', and after saying 'thank you for choosing S-Net' early at [15:44], you failed to include the closing branding in your final four turns.

scorecard.name: Hold time and Dead Air
scorecard.coaching: You left the customer in two unmanaged silences exceeding 30 seconds: a 48-second gap before [06:17] without proper hold phrasing and a 62-second silence before [09:37] where the customer had to ask if you were still there.

scorecard.name: Verified customer
scorecard.coaching: You did not request the customer's address and security PIN until [04:46], which was after the 240-second verification deadline had already passed.

scorecard.name: Active listening
scorecard.coaching: At [10:07], you asked the customer what error code was on the screen even though he had already told you 'CS-104' twice at [00:10] and [00:37] and you had looked up the CS-104 bulletin at [05:09].

scorecard.name: Took ownership of the problem
scorecard.coaching: At [15:00] and [17:21], you deflected responsibility to the TV hardware dispatch team and told the customer to ring back tomorrow morning himself instead of logging the replacement swap or arranging a follow-up.

scorecard.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
scorecard.coaching: The call ended at [17:57]–[18:47] with the Vision 4K box still stuck in the CS-104 boot loop, the iPad app blocked, and no replacement order booked.

grader.scenario: TV set-top box stuck in boot loop with error code CS-104 and missing sports channels
grader.notes: Poor-tier TV support call (score 40.0) with 6 FAILs and 5 PASSes. Megan shows genuine early empathy ([00:24]), paraphrases well ([00:51]), and probes physical cabling ([01:43]–[03:31]), but misses exact opening branding at [00:00] and buries closing branding early at [15:44] (B FAIL), verifies PIN late at [04:46] past 240s (V FAIL), leaves two unmanaged silences before [06:17] and [09:37] (H FAIL), forgets error code CS-104 at [10:07] (AL FAIL), deflects hardware replacement to another department at [15:00] (O FAIL), and leaves the box broken (RE FAIL).

items.name: Branding and Survey Check
items.evidence: Hard-case FAIL: Agent used informal 'thanks for calling S-Net' at [00:00] (missing exact 'thank you for calling S-Net') and delivered 'thank you for choosing S-Net' prematurely at [15:44] with eight subsequent Agent turns before the call ended at [18:47].

items.name: Hold time and Dead Air
items.evidence: Two unmanaged gaps >30s: 48s gap before [06:17] (preceded only by 'Hold on a sec' at [05:09] and no thank-you on return) and 62s gap before [09:37] where Customer chased with 'Hello? Are you still there, Megan?'.

items.name: Verified customer
items.evidence: Hard-case FAIL: Agent performed security verification (address and PIN), but only asked at [04:46] (past the 04:00 / 240s cutoff).

items.name: Personalized the call/ticket appropriately
items.evidence: Used the customer's name 'Tariq' regularly throughout the conversation (e.g., [00:24], [00:51], [04:46], [18:47]).

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: Hard-case PASS: Despite the poor overall outcome, Agent delivered a warm, genuine apology and empathy statement at [00:24] ('Oh no, Tariq, I am so sorry you're missing the football match tonight—I completely understand how frustrating it is').

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: Hard-case PASS: Restated the boot-loop symptoms in her own words and checked accuracy with the customer at [00:51].

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: Customer stated error code 'CS-104' at [00:10] and [00:37], yet Agent asked 'what was that error code on the screen again?' at [10:07].

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: Hard-case FAIL: At [15:00], Agent said 'Look, our TV hardware dispatch team handles faulty boxes, that's not something I deal with here—you'll have to ring them tomorrow morning to book a swap.'

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: Maintained a polite, non-hostile tone throughout the call even when the customer grew frustrated.

items.name: Probing
items.evidence: Asked appropriate hardware diagnostic questions covering mains power vs surge strip ([01:43]), Ethernet vs Wi-Fi ([02:04]), HDMI port ([02:26]), optical/USB peripherals ([02:49]), and LED boot colours ([03:31]).

items.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
items.evidence: At [17:57], Customer confirmed 'the box is still stuck restarting on my floor, I can't watch the match on my TV or my iPad, and I have to call another department tomorrow morning.'
